complex_roots_from_quadratic.display_name: Find complex roots of a quadratic via the quadratic formula

easy.statement_latex: Find the complex roots of the equation $x^2 - 4x + 13 = 0$. Give your answer in $a + bi$ form.
hints: Apply the quadratic formula $x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$. The discriminant is negative, so use $\sqrt{-k} = i\sqrt{k}$.
solution_steps_latex: Since the discriminant is negative, factor out $-1$: $\sqrt{-36} = 6i$.
